text:
jessica: Heads-up — canary showed a regression after the 'piecemeal quant' rollout. Short seq gen (<=16 tokens) lat went up ~9% on p50, p95 worse. Not huge but consistent across two regions.
liam: ugh. seen similar on the CI microbench. Did you repro locally?
jessica: yes, repro with local perf harness.
jessica: baseline (master-before-rollout) 8-token p50 21ms, after change 23ms. p95 48ms -> 54ms. numbers from perf-bot below.
perf-bot: benchmark summary: model=gpt-like, seq=8, batch=1, hw=gpu-a, runs=500, p50=23ms, p95=54ms, peak-mem=7.6GB
rachit: any changes in kernel selector heuristics? my recent patch added a fallback probe that tries int4 kernels for "low-variance" layers which adds a probe loop on first request.
liam: that probe is probably the culprit. it does per-layer dispatch checks and touches KV structures which can break warm cache locality.
sylvia: can you paste the probe snippet?
rachit: sure — the logic is basically: ```python
for layer in model.layers:
    if is_low_variance(layer.weights):
        try_use_int4 = probe_kernel(layer, sample_input)
```
rachit: probe_kernel runs a short forward and checks latency/accuracy delta, it's lightweight but runs synchronously on first request for each variant.
liam: synchronous per-layer probing on the hot path will add micro stalls and pollute the KV cache mapping. even if probe itself is fast, it changes memory access patterns.
jessica: profiling flamegraph attached (pasted): top shows kernel_selector::probe_loop ~7% CPU on short seqs, plus frequent kv_cache->evict calls increasing.
jessica: Quick profiler excerpt: ```
0. probe_loop: 7.1%
1. kernel_exec_int4: 35.6%
2. kv_cache_lookup: 12.4% (up from 4.1%)
3. batch_pack: 6.2%
```
liam: that kv_cache_lookup jump is worrying. maybe probe forces eviction because it allocates temp tensors on the same slab.
sylvia: quality-wise any regressions from skipping probe? we still need sensitivity mapping for per-layer quant.
rachit: we built sensitivity map from offline calibration runs — embedding and lm_head excluded by default. probe was an attempt to avoid large offline runs for every customer.
liam: suggestion: move probe off the hot path. do async probing on a sampled request or background warmup. also add a tiny persistent per-model flag so subsequent requests skip probe.
jessica: agree. for urgent rollback I can disable the probe via feature flag in the selector and re-run canary.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback-feature-quant-probe -> eng-runtime-canary (sha: a1b2c3d)
liam: also, consider changing batching heuristic: if a per-layer probe is detected/ongoing, avoid coalescing into tight batches that would exacerbate KV conflict. maybe we pause continuous batching for that model id for 1s.
sylvia: I'll run the quality eval on the offline sensitivity map with embeddings/lm_head excluded. If async probing goes in, we should still preserve the offline pass for final mapping.
rachit: action items: (1) liam add regression test that runs 1k short seq requests with the probe enabled (owner: liam), (2) jessica roll back probe in canary and remeasure (owner: jessica), (3) rachit implement async probe + persistent flag (owner: rachit), (4) sylvia validate offline mapping on our eval set and produce per-layer delta table (owner: sylvia). I'll open PRs.
liam: one more idea — we can avoid touching KV memory by running probe with an isolated allocator (temp arena) that doesn't allocate on the KV slab. cheaper and less invasive.
jessica: good point. for now I'll roll back and add metrics in the selector to count probe hits and probe latency. need numbers before re-enabling.
perf-bot: new run queued after rollback. will post results in 5m.
rachit: noted — async probe + isolated allocator probably best long-term. also refine the "low-variance" heuristic threshold, we might be over-eager and probing too many layers.
sylvia: i'll produce a CSV of per-layer sensitivity (delta perf vs delta quality) so we can set a cutoff.
liam: thanks everyone. short-term: rollback, add metrics, add test. medium-term: async probe + allocator + smarter thresholds + batching heuristic tweak to avoid KV thrash.
jessica: thanks — will follow up with canary numbers. :thumbsup:
